description: The INTO THE FRAY half of the 2026-08-27 'nothing happened' report. The roll-reporting fix is mode-agnostic — ChargeController routes on the dice context, not the mode — but Into the Fray has one thing Leap to Defend does not: 15.11 caps its charge roll at 6". The dice chips shown to the player are the RAW pair, so reporting only the capped total renders as "[2][6] = 6\"", which reads as broken arithmetic rather than as the rule working. This parks the Witchseekers 4" from the Warboss (inside the 6" Fray window, outside the 2" engagement range so the unit is still eligible), drives the REAL Into the Fray button, and asserts the raw 8 and the cap to 6 are both reported — dice log, Game Log and the movement prompt, which must clamp to the capped 6" and not the raw 8".

steps.comment: not required by Into the Fray (which ignores whether the target charged), but it keeps the board identical to the Leap scenario
4 inches edge-to-edge: inside INTO THE FRAY's 6 inch window, and still clear of the 2 inch engagement range so 15.11's 'unengaged' condition holds
guard the setup: a unit already in engagement range is not offered the window at all, and the rest would prove nothing

steps.script:
var d = tree.current_scene._phase_end_confirm
if d != null and d.visible:
	d.get_ok_button().pressed.emit()
return true

steps.comment: an enemy is within 6 inches, so INTO THE FRAY is live for this row

steps.equals: 2D6 charge (capped at 6") at the closest enemy within 6".
steps.comment: the live tooltip states the cap up front
the other mode's real button — the half of the report never previously driven
the counter-charge stands and the phase holds open for the move
15.11's cap is applied to the effective distance (raw 2+6=8 becomes 6) while the raw pair is kept — that mismatch is what the reporting has to explain
THE FIX, mode-specific half: the dice chips are the raw [2][6], so the dice log shows the raw 8" they add up to and then names the cap. Showing "[2][6] = 6\"" with no note reads as an arithmetic bug.
and the Game Log — which outlives the Charge phase — carries the same raw roll, cap and outcome

steps.comment: the movement prompt uses the CAPPED distance — the player must not be told they have 8" of counter-charge move
and the movement budget itself is the capped 6", not the raw roll
